title: Customers Spending leaves out a closed internal work order
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Open Reports > Customers Spending for today and note customer A's and customer B's figures.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer B.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, closed today, closed after the figures were noted.
  • Have a new work order for this test, work order 2, for customer B, invoiced today, billable, invoiced after the figures were noted, with line 1 at $240.00 and line 2 marked No Charge under Goodwill.
custom_steps:
1. Open Reports > Customers Spending.
  2. Set the date range to today.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The report opens.

Step 2:

  • Customer A's figure is the noted figure: work order 1 adds nothing.
  • Customer B's figure is the noted figure plus $240.00, the invoice total; line 2 adds $0.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11766 (Story 9, Reports, dashboard and exports)

  • S9-R15: “Reports not named above, checked and unchanged under rule zero: Requested Parts, Payroll Timesheet and the Journal Entries report (which shows the Close and no-charge-line entries with the category account on the debit side like any entry). Customers Spending excludes whole internal and no-charge work orders with the shared predicate of S9-R14; a billable work order with a no-charge line stays in with its invoice total, the line adds $0. Sales Follow Up and Vendors Expenses were removed from ShopView in v26.45.0 (SV-12106); if either returns, it takes the shared predicate then.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
